title: Zero-Copy Uploads
content:
Handling file uploads in Photon is incredibly efficient because we leverage Bun's native FormData handling which maps files to disk or memory without V8 heap allocation. This zero-copy approach provides exceptional performance for file uploads.

Why Zero-Copy Uploads?

Traditional Node.js file upload approaches (like Multer) require multiple memory copies:

  • 1File data serialized into JavaScript Buffer strings
  • 2Multiple memory allocations in V8 heap
  • 3Performance degradation with large files

Bun's native FormData and Bun.write() pass file descriptors directly to the optimized C++ layer, resulting in ~3x faster uploads with zero heap allocation.

Basic File Upload

The simplest way to handle file uploads:

import { Photon } from '@gravito/photon'
import path from 'node:path'

const app = new Photon()

app.post('/upload', async (c) => {
  const form = await c.req.formData()
  const file = form.get('file')
  
  if (!file || !(file instanceof File)) {
    return c.json({ error: 'No file provided' }, 400)
  }
  
  // Direct disk write (Zero-Copy)
  const uploadPath = path.join('uploads', file.name)
  await Bun.write(uploadPath, file)
  
  return c.json({
    success: true,
    filename: file.name,
    size: file.size,
    type: file.type
  })
})

Multiple File Upload

Handle multiple files in a single request:

app.post('/upload/multiple', async (c) => {
  const form = await c.req.formData()
  const files = form.getAll('files')
  
  const uploaded = []
  
  for (const file of files) {
    if (file instanceof File) {
      const uploadPath = path.join('uploads', file.name)
      await Bun.write(uploadPath, file)
      
      uploaded.push({
        filename: file.name,
        size: file.size,
        type: file.type
      })
    }
  }
  
  return c.json({ uploaded, count: uploaded.length })
})

File Validation

Security First

Always validate file size, type, and extension before saving to disk.

Validate files before processing:

// Validation helper function
function validateFile(file: File, options: {
  maxSize?: number
  allowedTypes?: string[]
  allowedExtensions?: string[]
}): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {
  const { maxSize = 10 * 1024 * 1024, allowedTypes = [], allowedExtensions = [] } = options
  
  // Check file size
  if (file.size > maxSize) {
    return { valid: false, error: `File size exceeds ${maxSize / 1024 / 1024}MB` }
  }
  
  // Check MIME type
  if (allowedTypes.length > 0 && !allowedTypes.includes(file.type)) {
    return { valid: false, error: `File type ${file.type} not allowed` }
  }
  
  // Check file extension
  const ext = path.extname(file.name).toLowerCase()
  if (allowedExtensions.length > 0 && !allowedExtensions.includes(ext)) {
    return { valid: false, error: `File extension ${ext} not allowed` }
  }
  
  return { valid: true }
}

// Usage in route
app.post('/upload/image', async (c) => {
  const form = await c.req.formData()
  const file = form.get('image')
  
  if (!file || !(file instanceof File)) {
    return c.json({ error: 'No file provided' }, 400)
  }
  
  // Validate file
  const validation = validateFile(file, {
    maxSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024, // 5MB
    allowedTypes: ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp'],
    allowedExtensions: ['.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png', '.webp']
  })
  
  if (!validation.valid) {
    return c.json({ error: validation.error }, 400)
  }
  
  // Generate unique filename
  const ext = path.extname(file.name)
  const uniqueName = `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).substring(7)}${ext}`
  const uploadPath = path.join('uploads', 'images', uniqueName)
  
  await Bun.write(uploadPath, file)
  
  return c.json({
    success: true,
    filename: uniqueName,
    url: `/uploads/images/${uniqueName}`
  })
})

Secure Filename Generation

Always sanitize and generate unique filenames to prevent security issues:

import crypto from 'node:crypto'

function generateSafeFilename(originalName: string): string {
  // Get file extension
  const ext = path.extname(originalName).toLowerCase()
  
  // Generate unique hash
  const hash = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex')
  
  // Sanitize original name (remove special characters)
  const sanitized = originalName
    .replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9.-]/g, '')
    .substring(0, 50) // Limit length
  
  // Combine: hash-originalname.ext
  return `${hash}-${sanitized}${ext}`
}

app.post('/upload/secure', async (c) => {
  const form = await c.req.formData()
  const file = form.get('file')
  
  if (!file || !(file instanceof File)) {
    return c.json({ error: 'No file provided' }, 400)
  }
  
  // Generate safe filename
  const safeName = generateSafeFilename(file.name)
  const uploadPath = path.join('uploads', safeName)
  
  await Bun.write(uploadPath, file)
  
  return c.json({
    success: true,
    filename: safeName,
    originalName: file.name
  })
})

File Upload with Additional Data

Handle file uploads with additional form fields:

app.post('/upload/with-data', async (c) => {
  const form = await c.req.formData()
  
  // Get file
  const file = form.get('file')
  
  // Get additional form fields
  const title = form.get('title') as string
  const description = form.get('description') as string
  const userId = form.get('userId') as string
  
  if (!file || !(file instanceof File)) {
    return c.json({ error: 'No file provided' }, 400)
  }
  
  // Save file
  const safeName = generateSafeFilename(file.name)
  const uploadPath = path.join('uploads', safeName)
  await Bun.write(uploadPath, file)
  
  // Save metadata to database (example with Atlas)
  // const record = await FileRecord.create({
  //   user_id: parseInt(userId),
  //   title,
  //   description,
  //   filename: safeName,
  //   original_name: file.name,
  //   size: file.size,
  //   mime_type: file.type
  // })
  
  return c.json({
    success: true,
    filename: safeName,
    metadata: { title, description }
  })
})

Progress Tracking (Client-Side)

Upload Progress

Use XMLHttpRequest or fetch with ReadableStream for upload progress tracking on the client side.

// Client-side example (HTML/JavaScript)
<form id="uploadForm">
  <input type="file" name="file" id="fileInput" />
  <button type="submit">Upload</button>
  <progress id="progress" value="0" max="100"></progress>
</form>

<script>
  document.getElementById('uploadForm').addEventListener('submit', async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    
    const formData = new FormData()
    const fileInput = document.getElementById('fileInput')
    formData.append('file', fileInput.files[0])
    
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest()
    
    xhr.upload.addEventListener('progress', (e) => {
      if (e.lengthComputable) {
        const percentComplete = (e.loaded / e.total) * 100
        document.getElementById('progress').value = percentComplete
      }
    })
    
    xhr.addEventListener('load', () => {
      if (xhr.status === 200) {
        console.log('Upload complete:', JSON.parse(xhr.responseText))
      }
    })
    
    xhr.open('POST', '/upload')
    xhr.send(formData)
  })
</script>

Error Handling

app.post('/upload/safe', async (c) => {
  try {
    const form = await c.req.formData()
    const file = form.get('file')
    
    if (!file || !(file instanceof File)) {
      return c.json({ error: 'No file provided' }, 400)
    }
    
    // Validate
    const validation = validateFile(file, {
      maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
      allowedTypes: ['image/jpeg', 'image/png']
    })
    
    if (!validation.valid) {
      return c.json({ error: validation.error }, 400)
    }
    
    // Save file
    const safeName = generateSafeFilename(file.name)
    const uploadPath = path.join('uploads', safeName)
    
    // Ensure upload directory exists
    await Bun.write(uploadPath, file)
    
    return c.json({
      success: true,
      filename: safeName
    })
    
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Upload error:', error)
    return c.json({
      error: 'Upload failed',
      message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'
    }, 500)
  }
})

Best Practices

  • ✓
    Always ValidateValidate file size, MIME type, and extension before saving
  • ✓
    Sanitize FilenamesGenerate unique, safe filenames to prevent path traversal attacks
  • ✓
    Set Size LimitsEnforce maximum file size limits to prevent DoS attacks
  • ✓
    Use WhitelistOnly allow specific file types and extensions (whitelist, not blacklist)
  • ✓
    Store MetadataSave file metadata (size, type, original name) to database for tracking
  • ✓
    Handle Errors GracefullyUse try-catch blocks and return appropriate error messages

Performance: This method is approximately 3x faster than Multer on Node.js because the file binary data is never serialized into a JS buffer string. Bun's native FormData handling maps files directly to disk or memory without V8 heap allocation, resulting in zero-copy uploads with exceptional performance.
